tracks.label: Start
tracks.tagline: Minimum Viable Method in about 10 minutes.
tracks.intro: The fastest reliable entry: classify the lane, choose one anchor, create only the next necessary artifact, and validate cheaply.

steps.narration: Start here for the lightest rigorous entry into the method: lane, anchor, next artifact, minimal validation, honest close-out.
Use the session guide only for the reduced start: classify the lane and avoid opening more process than the topic has earned.
Take one prompt and adapt it, but keep the Minimum Viable Method posture: smallest next artifact, no speculative ceremony.
If the topic is non-trivial, choose exactly one representation that removes ambiguity, not a bundle of diagrams by habit.

tracks.label: Discover
tracks.intro: A guided reading order across the core methodology pack. ~30 min for a first pass.

steps.narration: Start with the values: small, living, honest, proportional. They explain every choice that follows.
The end-to-end shape: Capture → Triage → Challenge → Promote → Design → Test → Gate → Implement → Close-out, plus three parallel lanes.
What 'design rigor without ceremony' looks like in practice: boundaries, mappings, decisions in the right scope.
How a vertical slice becomes a bounded execution unit (TB-*) with explicit exit criteria.
Risk-based test selection — minimum layers, optional layers, explicit non-coverage.
Mandatory checks at the gate: contracts, tests, docs, traceability.
How humans and AI work as peers in this method: bounded context, named skills, explicit handoffs.

tracks.label: Apply
tracks.tagline: Run a real slice from intake to close-out.
tracks.intro: A hands-on path: bootstrap a session, capture an idea, promote to a slice, design, test, gate, close out.

steps.narration: Bootstrap a session: read this, point the agent at the methodology pack, pick the starting skill.
Quick-start prompts: each one triggers a methodology skill (vision-intake, grill-me, tracer-bullet-promote, …).
Capture the idea as I-YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>. Keep the first version short and expressive.
If the idea is execution-ready, promote it to a TB-* with one vertical slice and an explicit first cut.
Use this template to bound the slice: scope, evidence, exit criteria, open questions that do not block.
Run global analysis, then component analysis for each impacted boundary.
One design brief per impacted component — boundaries, mappings, validation, error paths.
Select minimum and optional test layers explicitly. Risk-based, cost-aware.
Apply the gate, then close out: status transitions + traceability updates.

tracks.label: Present
tracks.tagline: A 7-beat narrative for a live methodology talk.
tracks.intro: Scenarized sequence with short talking points to support a live presentation of the method.

steps.narration: Beat 1 — Why this method exists. The lightest process that still preserves rigor, design consistency, and traceability.
Beat 2 — The end-to-end shape: one visible spine plus three parallel lanes (retrofit, plan incubation, multi-branch).
Beat 3 — The unit of execution: a tracer bullet — vertical, bounded, testable, promotable.
Beat 4 — Design discipline without ceremony: boundaries, mappings, decisions in the right scope.
Beat 5 — Quality is gated, not aspirational. Contracts, tests, docs, traceability.
Beat 6 — Humans and AI as peers: bounded context, named skills, explicit handoffs.
Beat 7 — Even legacy knowledge gets dignified treatment via R-* slices.
